receipts.sharp_question: How do we get website-form leads into Sugar reliably, subtracting Gravity Forms?

dewy_vector.D: Route website intake through Sugar's NATIVE Web-to-Lead (free, built-in) rather than Gravity Forms. Evidence: the real 'Web Site' leads carry the webtolead_email1 fingerprint (Sugar Web-to-Lead entry point) with no campaign; Gravity Forms posts to WordPress (prlresins.com/) and produced 0 Sugar leads in our ARCSTEST test. So a free native pipe already works and already produces the good leads; the contact form just isn't wired to it.
dewy_vector.E: Sugar Web-to-Lead form/entrypoint; the WordPress contact page (Josh's lane); Gravity Forms (subtract from the CRM path, keep or drop as UI).
dewy_vector.W: 1.2. Revisit after confirming what front-end currently feeds the working web-to-lead pipe.

receipts.true_north: Website leads land in Sugar reliably and for free, without the Gravity Forms / Akismet / reCAPTCHA / Mailgun tangle for the CRM write.
receipts.why: Subtract-GF, reuse-native, free. Sidesteps Akismet/reCAPTCHA/Mailgun for getting leads INTO Sugar (email notification stays a separate, smaller concern). Reuse-before-invent + cut-don't-add.
assumptions: The working 'Web Site' leads come via a Sugar-generated Web-to-Lead form (or a plugin posting to the endpoint) that we can reuse or regenerate
The native Web-to-Lead form can be embedded on the contact page (small WordPress change, Josh) with a honeypot/captcha for spam
receipts.wrong_if: The working web-to-lead leads actually originate FROM Gravity Forms posting to the endpoint (then GF isn't cleanly subtractable); OR the native form can't be styled/spam-protected acceptably for the site.
receipts.confidence: MEDIUM — evidence that Sugar Web-to-Lead is the working pipe is strong (webtolead_email1 fingerprint); the 'which front-end feeds it' + the WordPress embed are unconfirmed.
